title: Germany-wide cluster randomized controlled trial in pediatric and adolescent medical practices for the prevention and treatment of dysregulated screen media use
summary:
According to study results, high media consumption and the associated long screen time have a negative impact on children's development and health.  
The study “Screen-free – Take part!” aims to empower parents by providing them with information on how to limit their children's screen time in an age-appropriate manner. The participating pediatric practices are divided into an intervention group and a control group. In the intervention group, a sticker with the three most important recommendations for children's screen media use is placed in the examination booklet during the U7a examination to reinforce the pediatrician's advice. In addition, pediatricians will advise parents whose children have excessive screen time (60 minutes per day or more) in an intensive 15-minute media coaching session. The control group will receive treatment as usual.  
Before the U7a, parents fill out a questionnaire in the practice app ("Meine pädiatrische Praxis") about screen time, their child's development, their own internet use, and family activities. The questionnaire reveals whether the child has excessive or normal screen time. After 3, 6, and 9 months, the parents answer a question about their child's screen time at the pediatrician's office. About a year later, before the U8 examination, the complete questionnaire is filled out again in the PraxisApp.

interventions.name: Intervention group (normal), cluster randomization of pediatric practices. Children aged 32 months and older and their parents with screen time of less than 60 minutes per day in the pre-intervention survey receive education on age-appropriate screen media use at the U7a examination.

Intervention group (excessive), cluster randomization of pediatric practices. Children aged 32 months and older and their parents who reported screen time of 60 minutes or more per day in the pre-intervention survey receive education on age-appropriate screen media use at the U7a examination and app
Control group, cluster randomization of pediatric practices. Children aged 32 months and older and their parents receive treatment as usual at the U7a examination.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Visit to the U7a examination at a participating pediatric practice.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to consent, no PraxisApp.
